faqs.q: What should I do if I want to appeal a fine?
faqs.a: You can pay the fine, or you can find more information about going to court for a fine. Legal Aid NSW also has an online tool to help you work out the best way to deal with your legal problem.

faqs.q: Where can I get legal help and support?
faqs.a: You can contact an organization that offers legal help and support. Special court support services are available for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, and you can get help with translation or disability support.

faqs.q: How can I represent myself in court?
faqs.a: Representing yourself in court gives you access to your case information, allows you to file documents, and manages your profile in the NSW Courts and Tribunals services.

faqs.q: What do I need to know about the court process?
faqs.a: Information is available on what to wear, the people you will see, and how to behave inside a courtroom (Attending the Local Court). You can also learn about the court journey, and what to know about charges, bail, and appearing in court (Going to court as a defendant).
